pa_i_numero_uno_sector.blurb: A short stretch of wall on the Safe Harbor South rail-trail cliffs, the eighth sector as you head north from the Green Hill Road tunnel, along the Susquehanna near Lancaster. It holds 18 routes, mostly bolted single-pitch sport lines with a few trad cracks and one top-rope. Grades start at 5.6 and cluster in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, with a handful of 5.11s and one 5.12 for the strong. The climbing is at its best for people comfortable on moderate face and crack lines, and the shaded or sunny feel depends on the season, so cooler months suit it best.
pa_i_numero_uno_sector.parking_note: Leave the car near the tunnel on Green Hill Road, where room is limited, then follow the climbers' trail up to the rail trail and walk north to the sector.

pa_2_0_international_area.blurb: A tall, narrow band of rock beside the Susquehanna at the two-mile marker of the Safe Harbor North rail trail, south of Lancaster. The 18 routes are mostly bolted sport, with a couple of top-ropes and two trad lines. Grades run from 5.6 up to a single 5.12, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.10, so there are warm-ups as well as some firm tests. Expect a walk of a couple of miles on flat trail to reach it, and bring a 60 m rope since lines here can be long compared with the southern cliffs.
pa_2_0_international_area.approach: Walk or bike about two miles along the level rail trail from the north lot to the 2.0 marker, or start from the Chestnut Grove lot and head north along the trail beside the river.

pa_rim_rock.blurb: A small sandstone outcrop and boulder area in the Allegheny National Forest of northwest Pennsylvania, near Warren and the overlook above the reservoir. About half of the 18 routes are boulder problems, with the rest split evenly between top-rope and trad lines. Problems run from V0 to about V6, while the roped lines range from 5.7 into the 5.11 range. Protection on the rock is awkward, so top-roping is the practical way to climb the face. The hillside below holds plenty of bouldering, and there is room to explore beyond the established problems.
